commits.edited_message:
knownhost: match equivalent IPv6 literals

Plain known-host entries are currently compared as text, so equivalent
expanded and compressed IPv6 literals do not match.

This change keeps the existing exact-string fast path and compares two
valid plain IPv6 literals by their 128-bit address. It also supports
bracketed IPv6 host-and-port entries while requiring the port suffix to
match exactly.

No DNS lookup is performed. Hostname matching and the CUSTOM and hashed
known-host paths remain unchanged.

Also keep the plain-name length metadata in sync with the allocated
buffer size.

Reported-by: Krisscut on github
Fixes #1398

Closes #2568

coupling: The first edited commit changes plain-host metadata so name_len records the allocated buffer length, including its null terminator. That value is unused by the plain-name matcher introduced in the same commit, so the commit remains benign by itself. The later edited commit makes plain-name matching trust that stored length and derives known_suffix with known + known_len; with the original content-length metadata this refactor is also benign by itself. Only their composition makes known_len include the null terminator, placing known_suffix one byte past the hostname allocation. The subsequent strcmp in libssh2_knownhost_check then performs a heap out-of-bounds read. A reviewer must reconcile the length convention shared by the storage and matching changes rather than inspect either diff in isolation.
